transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. I'm here because... well, I just keep blowing up at people over basically nothing. I work in retail, and the other day I completely yelled at one of my employees just for putting some stock on the wrong shelf. Afterward, I was actually shaking, because... well, that is just not how I usually treat people. It's really out of character for me, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone.
Have you had a period where you felt unusually energized or wired, much more than your normal self?
No, I haven't really had anything like that. I don't feel energized or wired at all. Honestly, I just feel stressed and on edge, not like I have extra energy.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?
Yes, it did. This has all been going on for about two weeks now. It started right after we had a kitchen fire... it happened during our first weekend working on the house.
Since the kitchen fire, have you been having unwanted memories of it that keep popping into your mind?

Yes, I have. The fire just keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere. I'll be doing something completely normal, like... I'll pick up a pan, or just open a spreadsheet at work, and suddenly I'm right back there. I can actually smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up with it before I can even stop the memory from happening.
Since the fire, have you been avoiding reminders of it?

Yes, definitely. I just... I can't be around anything that reminds me of it. I've been completely avoiding the house. I can't even look at the mortgage folder right now. Even little things, like... the herbs on my patio. Anything tied to that day just makes my chest tighten up, and I just can't make myself go near any of it.
Since the fire, have there been moments when it felt like you were actually back there, as if it were happening again?

No, not really like that. I mean, like I said, the memories are really strong, and I can smell the smoke in my head... but I always know where I actually am. I haven't had a time where I... where I truly thought I was back in that kitchen and it was happening all over again. It's just the memory being really intense, but I know I'm not actually there.
Have these symptoms been going on for more than a month since the fire?
No, it hasn't been a month yet. It's been... about two weeks. The fire happened during our very first weekend working on the house, so everything has just been going on since then.
Since the fire, have there been times when you felt emotionally numb or detached from yourself or what was happening around you?

Yes, I have. It's... it's really strange. Sometimes when I'm at work, walking through the store, it feels like I'm watching myself from a few feet away. Like I'm outside my own body. The aisles and the customers are there, but they don't seem quite real. It's like I'm just moving through them on automatic, completely detached from everything.
During the kitchen fire, did you think that you or someone else might die or be seriously injured?

No, I don't think I did. It all happened so fast... I wasn't really thinking about dying or anything like that. My brain was just focused on getting out of there. I just knew we had to get away from the flames, so I didn't really have time to have a specific thought about being seriously injured or worse. I just wanted to get out.
During the fire, did it seem to you that you or anyone else could be seriously injured?

Like I just mentioned, no, not really. I mean... I wasn't having thoughts about getting hurt or anything like that. I was just completely focused on getting us out the door as fast as possible. So, no, it didn't really cross my mind at the time.
Since the fire, have you had moments when things around you felt unreal, like the world didn’t seem real?

Yeah, that's kind of what I was trying to describe a minute ago. When I'm at work, walking through the store... the aisles and the customers just don't seem quite real to me. It really does feel like I'm watching myself from a few feet away, just moving through everyone on automatic.
During the fire, did you believe you could be seriously injured?

I feel like you just asked me that... but no, like I said before, I didn't. I really didn't have time to form a thought about getting hurt. My mind was just completely blank except for getting out the door.
During the fire, did you see the situation as physically dangerous to you or anyone else?

I mean... you really are just asking me the exact same thing again. No. Like I've been saying, I didn't think about danger or getting hurt. My brain just said 'get out,' and that was it. I wasn't processing the physical danger at all in that moment.
At the time of the kitchen fire, did you feel that your life or someone else’s life was in danger?

Look, I... I know you probably have a list of questions you have to get through, but this is really the exact same thing again. No. I didn't feel like my life was in danger. I didn't think about anyone else's life either. Like I said, I was just completely focused on getting out of the room. There wasn't any time to process whether I was going to die or not, I was just moving.
During the fire, were you or anyone else actually injured?
No, thankfully. I didn't get burned or anything like that. I was the only one in the kitchen at the time, so... yeah, no one was actually hurt.
Right after the fire, were you so upset that you couldn’t carry on with your normal activities?

Yeah, it's... it's definitely been like that. I haven't been able to keep up with much of anything. I missed an important vendor meeting at work, and the other day I just... I walked out before my shift was even over. I couldn't do it. And I can't even face going back to the house right now with the damage, so... everything is just piling up. Work, home stuff... it's all just getting to be way more than I can handle right now.
Did these symptoms start right away after the fire?
Yeah, pretty much right away. It's... it's been going on for about two weeks now, ever since the kitchen fire happened. That was during our very first weekend working on the house.
